reading.body:
AI business interruption is being underwritten as a power risk: four of the ten coverage categories concern grid supply, water, or interconnection, not software.

The ten categories split into three kinds of failure. Four are power and grid risks: utility load shedding and throttling, power purchase agreement failure, drought-related water shutoffs, and interconnection queue delay. Two are network risks: subsea fibre cuts and dark fibre backhaul disruption. Four are service and software risks: hyperscaler outage cascades, GPU provider service level breaches, foundational API outages, and edge node update corruption.

The power group is what separates this from ordinary IT downtime cover. Interconnection queue delay protects against a grid connection date slipping by years, which is a permitting and construction exposure rather than an operating one. Power purchase agreement failure covers an independent producer not delivering contracted megawatts on schedule. Both sit upstream of the data centre, where compute depends on the building and the supply behind it. Concentration runs alongside: contingent business interruption for a hyperscaler outage, foundational API outages, and GPU provider service level breaches all describe many downstream users exposed to one provider's failure.

What the data does not contain is any measure of cost or frequency. There are no premiums, limits, retentions, or paid claims, and every entry's source field is empty, so none of it is tied to a policy wording or a loss event. It is a list of what the market is naming as insurable, not evidence of what it has paid out or how often these events occur. It also does not say who buys these products, or whether they are available at all.
